newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CBA forges higher on dividend, buyback talk.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CBA forges higher on dividend, buyback talk.

text.p: Shares in the Commonwealth Bank of Australia forged to yet another all-time high in early Monday trade as retail investors in particular bought on talk that the bank may issue a special dividend or buy back shares to return excess capital.
CBA was up 13 cents at A$12.69 at 11.15 a.m. (0015 GMT), off an all-time high of A$12.75 hit in earlier trade, but well above its 1997 base set on January 2 of A$11.99.
But banking analysts said they were doubtful about the talk of a special dividend, even though the bank appeared to have excess franking credits to offload.
"The potential for a special dividend is there, but I don't think that is what they'll do," said one senior Sydney banking analyst, adding that a buyback was more likely.
"Retail investors love this talk of a special dividend and the retail brokers are pushing it," the analyst said.
He said any buy-back, however, would be unlikely to rival CBA's 10 percent buy-back staged last year in conjunction with the float of the government's remaining 50.4 percent stake in the bank.
Another Sydney banking analyst said he doubted the bank would use the excess capital for either a buyback or a special dividend.
"Whilst they have a capacity to undertake a buy-back, they have A$1.6 billion of quasi-tier one capital (dated bonds and notes on issue) that they need to refinance," the analyst said.

Analysts also said CBA's share price tended to rise in the period just before results and its hefty dividends were announced. CBA is expected to announce its interim dividend in February. -- Bernard Hickey, Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1812
